root_cause.text: In the KVM nSVM nested state restore path (`svm_set_nested_state`), a `WARN_ON_ONCE` was placed on `nested_svm_load_cr3()` failure, but this failure is trivially triggerable by userspace by setting CPUID properties after loading CR3, allowing a user-triggerable kernel warning.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `WARN_ON_ONCE`, and the commit message explicitly states that modifying CPUID after loading CR3 (e.g., setting `CR3` bit 44 then limiting `MAX_PHY_ADDR` to 36) causes the warning to fire in `svm_set_nested_state`. The example code in the description demonstrates the exact userspace sequence that triggers it.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove WARN_ON_ONCE from nested_svm_load_cr3 failure path to avoid spurious kernel warnings when the failure is expected.
intent_record.what: Removed the WARN_ON_ONCE wrapper from the condition check on the return value of nested_svm_load_cr3, changing 'if (WARN_ON_ONCE(ret))' to 'if (ret)'.
intent_record.how: When nested_svm_load_cr3 fails, the code will no longer emit a kernel warning (once) before jumping to the error path; it will silently handle the error.
